title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Maiolica: the invitation as a hand-painted Tuscan ceramic panel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Maiolica
options.lineage: Hand-painted tin-glaze tiles of Vietri, Deruta and Montelupo
options.thesis: The invitation is a hand-painted ceramic panel: tiles carry the page and glaze carries every state.
materials: milky tin glaze with brush drag
unglazed biscuit terracotta for empty states
cobalt line borders painted by hand
options.viewport: On a phone: the names painted inside one cobalt-framed tile panel with a lemon-and-leaf border, date and villa on the panel foot, the reply tile directly under it.
options.risk: Slides into souvenir-shop kitsch if motifs multiply; it must hold two motifs and one strict tile module.

raised.raise: One state language: an unchosen option is bare biscuit terracotta, a chosen one fills with glaze.
Each day of the weekend owns one glaze: Friday saffron, Saturday cobalt, Sunday copper green.
Everything snaps to one tile module; small screens drop columns, never the tile size.
Cobalt commits a third of every viewport, and rank comes from how many tiles an element spans.
The tile grid runs unbroken under the whole page as one continuous floor.
Finished reply steps keep a painted tick on their tile, so progress stays on the surface.

options.label: Svatební oznámení
options.lineage: The folded Czech wedding announcement card with its reply slip
options.thesis: The site is the printed oznámení your grandmother keeps on the shelf, with the reply slip torn off and sent back.
options.viewport: A single folded card opening on screen: names in fine roman caps, date line, and a perforated reply slip below the fold.
options.risk: This is where most wedding sites land: cream card, serif caps, muted gold. Trusted and familiar, but generic.

options.label: Akari Lantern Workshop
options.lineage: Washi and bamboo folded light sculptures
options.thesis: Every section is a paper lantern that lights up when you reach it.
options.viewport: Glowing paper volumes hanging at different heights, the names on the brightest one.
options.case: Fuses as a lantern-lit dinner, but Czech guests at a Tuscan villa do not recognise a Japanese workshop.
options.kept: One clear state language: lit means chosen.
options.risk: Reads as a foreign theme with no tie to the couple or the place.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.lineage: Surreal night cities folding into quilts
options.thesis: The weekend as a city that folds into a blanket at night.
options.viewport: A night city map folding over a park, districts tinted by weather.
options.case: Poetic, but an outdoor Tuscan country weekend is not a city at night; clarity suffers.
options.kept: Each district owns its own hue.
options.risk: Guests would have to decode a metaphor to find the date.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: The invitation as windows on a one-bit desktop.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows with the names in a title bar.
options.case: Witty for tech friends, alienating for grandparents and wrong for a romantic weekend.
options.kept: Strict whole-module scale with nothing off grid.
options.risk: Reads as a joke rather than an invitation.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.lineage: Film editing bench with a perforated select rail
options.thesis: Each part of the weekend as a frame strung on a film rail.
options.viewport: A perforated rail across an orange field, the ceremony frame flagged.
options.case: Strong system, but guests do not identify with an editing bench and the dark orange field fights a garden wedding.
options.kept: One ink holds a third of every screen; rank by cell count.
options.risk: Feels like a film-festival site, not a wedding.

options.label: Grid Horizon Sunset
options.thesis: Driving toward a striped sunset on a neon grid.
options.viewport: Extruded names over a banded sun on the horizon.
options.case: Only the sunset overlaps with Tuscany; the neon world erases the place.
options.kept: One continuous grid that keeps arriving underneath.
options.risk: Retro novelty that guests would not connect to the couple.

options.label: Flash Scrawl Sleeve
options.lineage: French house record sleeves defaced with marker
options.thesis: A party photo scrawled over with the couple's names.
options.viewport: A flash photo with the names drawn over it in marker.
options.case: Energetic, but there are no real photos of the couple yet and the club register misfits older guests.
options.kept: Used marks stay on the surface as history.
options.risk: Depends entirely on photography that does not exist.

canonCard.label: The wedding-site standard
canonCard.thesis: What every wedding website template ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A full-screen couple photo with script names, a countdown, detail cards and an RSVP form.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every template by design.
